answer: Because the grove forfeiture is applied at exit, the mesa ledger totals each burn, and the relic audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 161 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 86% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned so that nobody profits from it. That is 24 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
